page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-intensive and machine learning workloads. The hardware configuration features 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC 9575F cores on a shared allocation model, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192 GB of RAM, translating to 12 GB of memory per core. Graphics and parallel processing power are driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage, meaning external storage volumes must be attached.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance remains strong, ranking in the top 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write speeds are also positioned in the top 25%. In language model benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier inference speeds for small 135M models, while maintaining strong to average performance when processing medium 7B and large 70B models.

This server configuration is optimized for workloads requiring heavy parallel processing and high memory capacity. It is highly suited for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and rendering tasks. The combination of AMD EPYC processors and dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs provides a highly capable environment for enterprise-grade AI workloads, though users must plan for external storage integration.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server designed for high-compute and machine learning workloads. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 192 GB of system memory, and two NVIDIA L40S GPUs with a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Running on the KVM hypervisor, the x86_64 architecture delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities. While local storage is not included, the system excels in memory bandwidth and data processing benchmarks. This server is highly suited for LLM inference, data science, and parallel computing tasks that leverage dedicated hardware acceleration.
